new_entities.name: Coffee enema
new_entities.description: Rectal instillation of coffee promoted in detox or alternative-medicine protocols.

new_entities.name: Human outcomes
new_entities.description: Overall clinically meaningful outcomes reported in human use, including benefit, harm, or lack of validated efficacy.

edges.effect_quant: A 2020 systematic review of coffee-enema case reports found no studies demonstrating effectiveness and identified nine adverse-event reports, including multiple colitis cases. A 34-patient pilot study for bowel preparation found feasibility without major immediate complications in that narrow endoscopy setting, but this does not validate broader wellness or detox claims.
edges.population: people using coffee enemas for self-care, detoxification, or alternative-medicine purposes
edges.mechanism: Promoters claim bile flow or glutathione-related detox enhancement, but those mechanistic claims have not translated into convincing human outcome evidence.
edges.summary: This is a contested and safety-limited edge rather than a legitimate wellness therapy. The clinical literature offers essentially no proof of broad benefit, while documented harms range from colitis to septicemia.
edges.caveats: The one small endoscopy-prep pilot is not evidence for systemic detox, metabolic improvement, or general health benefit. Most of the stronger literature around coffee enemas centers on adverse events, not efficacy.

evidence.notes: The safety and effectiveness of self-administered coffee enema: A systematic review of case reports.

evidence.citation: Kim ES et al 2014 Clin Nutr Res
evidence.notes: Coffee enema for preparation for small bowel video capsule endoscopy: a pilot study.
